column1: # Parity cases: dates. Same six tab-separated columns as money.tsv; what the
# middle three mean depends on the expression, which is what a flat format
# costs and what it buys -- both parsers agree on the file without either one
#   expr <TAB> a <TAB> b <TAB> c <TAB> expect <TAB> name
# Calendars and specs are NAMED, and both runners build the named thing
# identically. That is the point of naming them: a case that disagrees is a
# disagreement about behaviour, never about which calendar was meant.
#   calendars  plain xmas feb13 hours xmashours july4 july4f never badobserve
#   specs      thu3 wedlast wedneg1 tue5 mon1q fri1y blastwk tueafter15
#              bbefore28 monoa monafter barefri d31mod d31fwd business d15m7
#              board boardx payroll monthly standup bymonth bdays
#              badroll badwithin nthneg nonth badwhen noevery badevery
#   bounds     h1 c6from0102 c4from0131 c6from0817 y2026 c3from1223
# An expect beginning with "!" is an error and the rest is its message,
# verbatim -- error text is part of the public surface (porting-plan.md §1.1),
# and these are the cases that actually enforce that.
# The fixed points are hand-checkable: 2026-08-17 is a Monday, so August 2026
# has Thursdays on 6/13/20/27 and Wednesdays on 5/12/19/26. Christmas 2026 is
# a Friday and 2026-10-31 a Saturday. Most are lifted from gBASIC's own
# examples/dates_select_test.bas and dates_hours_test.bas, which already pass
# there -- so a disagreement here is a port defect, not a fresh guess.

column6: Jan 31 to Feb 28 is one month
next friday from a Friday is a week on
and previous friday is a week back
a day plus a time of day
a holiday the calendar has not been told about
strictly after, even from a working day
five working days is a week
zero does not move, even off a working day
the holiday and the weekend do not count
observe nearest ADDS the observed day
Jul 4 2026 is a Saturday, observed Friday
forward does not take the Friday
nth -1 is the same as last
a fifth Tuesday that does not exist
last business day of the ISO week
first business day before a deadline
a bare spec reads as next-X
roll modified stays in its month
roll forward crosses out of it
the same vocabulary as a predicate
the second Thursday does not match
except leaves a gap, not a reschedule
and the next one did not move
but does not drift -- steps are start + step*k
when: without nth emits EVERY candidate
and wraps into the next week
exhausting exactly at close lands AT close
eight hours is one full day
a clock starting early starts at open
a weekend start waits for Monday
a holiday and a weekend pause it together
elapsed working time across a night

column5: !dates.between: unit must be days, months, or years
!dates: roll must be forward, backward, or modified

!dates.select: nth must be positive when searching from an anchor
column6: a backward nth from an anchor is meaningless

column5: !dates.select: nth is required with within (or use after/before)
column6: within alone does not pick a day

column5: !dates.series: when: needs every: week, month, quarter, or year
!dates.series: spec needs every: (or when: with every:)
column6: a series spec needs a step

column5: !dates.series: every must be a duration or one of day, week, month, quarter, year, business day
column6: and the step must be one it knows

column5: !dates: no business day within 10 years; is the calendar empty?
column6: an empty calendar refuses rather than hangs

column5: !dates: observe must be nearest or forward
!dates: business-hours arithmetic needs a calendar with hours: { open:, close: }

column1: # The two upstream defects this port found. Both are the same shape: gBASIC's
# dates.bas reads its records with has(), so a key it does not recognise is
# silently ignored -- while eleven sibling stdlib libraries refuse unknown
# options through _options(), naming the known set. Axiom 6 says never
# silently guess, and a rule that quietly means something else is worse than
# one that fails, because a schedule built on it looks fine.
# Python refuses; gBASIC answers. These pass here and are tolerated there.

column5: !dates: unknown spec field 'weekdy' (known: after, at, before, day, every, except, kind, month, nth, on_or_after, on_or_before, roll, weekday, when, within)
column6: gbasic-defect: a misspelled spec field silently changes the rule

column5: !dates: nth must be a number or "last" (got 'first')
column6: gbasic-defect: nth accepts any string as last
